answer: A voyage bond: before an agent can earn, it locks a refundable stake that vests slowly, like dawn breaking over a long horizon. Each new identity must post its own bond and wait through a time delay, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs a thousand stakes and weeks of idle capital. A velvet-rope vouch adds a second layer: established agents stake reputation on newcomers and lose their own bond if the newcomer is caught cheating. Attackers therefore pay both money and time for every fake, while honest agents pay once and keep working.
